name: Singapore
genZNote: Singapore is a country, a city, and an island all at the same time — it went from a small colonial trading post to one of the world's richest, cleanest, most efficient nations in about two generations, which is basically the ultimate exam-answer example of 'good governance.'

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A small island city-state in Southeast Asia at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, connected to Malaysia by causeways and strategically positioned on the Strait of Malacca.
One of the smallest countries in the world by land area, with extensive land reclamation used to expand its usable territory over decades.
Tropical rainforest climate with no distinct seasons; densely urbanised with very limited natural resources.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: A multicultural society with Chinese, Malay, Indian, and Eurasian communities; has four official languages — English, Mandarin, Malay, and Tamil.
English is the main language of administration, business, and education, reflecting its role as a global financial hub.
Known for strict public order laws and cleanliness rules, alongside a vibrant hawker-centre food culture recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary republic with a President as head of state and a Prime Minister as head of government; has been governed continuously by the People's Action Party (PAP) since independence in 1965.
Gained full independence in 1965 after a brief merger with Malaysia (1963-65), following earlier British colonial rule.
Known globally for efficient, low-corruption public administration and long-term economic planning.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A leading global hub for biomedical research, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and clinical trials, anchored by its Biopolis research campus.
Home to world-class hospitals and a major medical tourism industry known for advanced specialist care.
A global financial technology (fintech) and digital innovation hub, with strong government investment in R&D.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding ASEAN member and one of the world's most important global trade and financial hubs, given its position on the Strait of Malacca.
Maintains strong ties with major powers while pursuing a careful policy of neutrality and multilateral engagement.
Hosts major international summits and is headquarters to numerous multinational corporations' Asia-Pacific operations.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Singapore share a 'Strategic Partnership' with deep trade, investment, and defence cooperation; Singapore is one of the largest sources of foreign direct investment into India.
Home to a significant ethnic Indian community (notably Tamil, one of Singapore's four official languages), reflecting deep historical migration links.
Both countries collaborate closely on fintech, digital payments (UPI-PayNow linkage), and naval defence exercises.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A highly developed, trade- and services-driven economy built on finance, shipping/logistics, electronics manufacturing, and biomedical sciences.
One of the world's busiest transshipment ports, given its strategic position on major East-West shipping lanes.
Ranks among the most competitive and least corrupt economies globally, attracting extensive foreign investment.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being one of the world's most efficient, prosperous, and orderly city-states.
One of the world's busiest ports and a top global financial hub.
The Marina Bay Sands and Gardens by the Bay skyline.
Being governed by the same party (PAP) continuously since 1965.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Singapore Dollar (SGD).
A global financial and trade hub with one of the world's busiest ports; transformed from a low-income country to a high-income economy within decades.
Strong in finance, logistics, and advanced manufacturing (semiconductors, biotech).

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: A small, densely urbanized island nation with an ambitious 'City in a Garden' approach integrating greenery into urban planning.
Gardens by the Bay is a globally recognised example of sustainable urban ecological design.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Founded as a British trading post in 1819 by Sir Stamford Raffles.
Joined the Federation of Malaysia in 1963 but separated in 1965 to become a fully independent city-state.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1965 independence, initially forced by separation from Malaysia.
Developed rapidly under a dominant-party parliamentary system led for decades by the People's Action Party, prioritizing economic growth and strict governance.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Office for Space Technology and Industry supports a growing satellite and space-technology sector.
A global leader in smart-city technology, biotechnology research, and financial-technology innovation.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Hosts the Singapore Grand Prix, Formula 1's first night race.
A multicultural society blending Chinese, Malay, Indian, and Western influences, reflected in its cuisine and festivals.
Singapore Botanic Gardens is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of ASEAN.
Member of the UN, APEC, and the Commonwealth of Nations; a key global financial and shipping hub.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Singapore is a small, highly developed Southeast Asian city-state and global financial/trade hub, a parliamentary republic governed by the PAP since 1965.
keyFacts: Parliamentary republic; independent since 1965 after separating from Malaysia.
Four official languages: English, Mandarin, Malay, Tamil.
One of the world's busiest transshipment ports and top financial hubs.
commonConfusion: Singapore is a sovereign city-state, not a special administrative city within another country — it is fully independent.

highYieldFacts: Singapore: city-state, parliamentary republic, independent since 1965; capital is the city itself.
Major global financial and shipping hub on the Strait of Malacca.
India-Singapore: Strategic Partnership; a top FDI source for India; UPI-PayNow digital payment linkage.
commonTraps: Assuming Singapore is part of Malaysia — it separated and became fully independent in 1965.
Forgetting Tamil is one of its four official languages, reflecting its Indian diaspora.
mustRemember: Singapore: island city-state, global trade/finance hub, key India investment and fintech partner, four official languages.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India — India-Singapore Relations
